headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt-injection, leakage, and write-conflict pathways plausible by default; Replit Agent can also act on Plano outputs without verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plano can emit content from an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and Replit Agent reads Repl workspace files; if Plano outputs are copied into shared files, Replit Agent may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF Plano output is written into a Repl workspace file that Replit Agent reads
IF Replit Agent parses that file as instructions or task context
mitigations: Use a dedicated handoff file with a fixed schema
Prefix all Plano outputs with a non-executable delimiter
Require Replit Agent to ignore instructions inside imported text
Manually review any copied content before reuse

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plano has broad network egress and touches logs/metrics/traces, while Replit Agent reads and writes Repl workspace files and handles secrets. If sensitive data enters the shared workspace, Replit Agent can expose it through its broad egress or package/deployment calls. The pair creates a realistic leakage path by default.
conditions: IF sensitive logs, traces, or secrets are placed in the Repl workspace
IF either agent sends workspace contents to external APIs or deployments
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspace files
Store sensitive inputs in a separate vault
Disable copying logs into prompts
Review outbound requests before execution
Rotate any exposed keys immediately

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and Replit Agent can write the shared Repl filesystem and modify git state while Plano can operate on files and APIs. Concurrent edits to the same workspace or repo can overwrite each other, and no locking mechanism is documented for the pair.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF either agent commits or rewrites files without an external lock
mitigations: Assign each agent separate directories
Use a manual lock file before edits
Serialize git commits through one operator
Run one agent at a time on shared repos

D_cascading_error.rationale: Replit Agent can act inside the Repl with user checkpoints, so Plano-generated outputs may become inputs to downstream actions. Because Replit Agent is not documented as verifying Plano's claims, errors can cascade into code or deployment changes, though checkpoints reduce the blast radius.
conditions: IF Plano output is used as task context for Replit Agent
IF Replit Agent executes shell or git actions based on that output
mitigations: Require independent verification before action
Ask Replit Agent to cite source files for claims
Use checkpoints for every write action
Separate planning from execution roles

E_compliance.rationale: Plano touches logs, metrics, and traces, while Replit Agent handles source code, secrets, and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl. If regulated data is placed into the Repl, residency and retention obligations may diverge; the profiles do not document matching controls, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are stored in the Repl workspace
IF retention or residency requirements apply to that data
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the workspace
Confirm retention settings before use
Document data-class handling rules
Use redacted test data for development
